name: Transport dispatch
description: How a guest call reaches a host object, what crosses in each direction, and how long a capability reference lasts.

scenarios.title: An answer the wire cannot carry becomes a reference to it
given: a bound Service whose method answers a stateful object
scenarios.when: the guest calls it
scenarios.then: the guest receives a capability reference rather than the object

scenarios.title: An answer the wire can carry crosses as itself
given: a bound Service whose method answers a primitive
scenarios.when: the guest calls it
scenarios.then: the guest receives that value, not a reference

scenarios.title: A reference passed as a positional argument arrives as its object
given: a guest holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: it passes the reference as a positional argument to a Service
scenarios.then: the Service receives the host object

scenarios.title: A reference passed as a keyword argument arrives as its object
given: a guest holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: it passes the reference as a keyword argument to a Service
scenarios.then: the Service receives the host object

scenarios.title: A reference the table never issued is refused as an argument
given: an invocation whose Handle table never issued a given id
scenarios.when: the guest passes that id as an argument
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: A reference used as the receiver dispatches to its object
given: a guest holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: it calls a method on that reference
scenarios.then: the host object answers

scenarios.title: An answer from a reference is referenced in turn
given: a guest holding a capability reference whose method answers a stateful object
scenarios.when: it calls that method
scenarios.then: the guest receives a new capability reference

scenarios.title: A reference the table never issued is refused as a receiver
given: an invocation whose Handle table never issued a given id
scenarios.when: the guest calls a method on that id
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: References are numbered from one, upward
given: a fresh Handle table
scenarios.when: several references are allocated in turn
scenarios.then: their ids run upward from one

scenarios.title: A reference answers with the object it was made for
given: a Handle table holding one allocation
scenarios.when: that id is fetched
scenarios.then: it answers the object that was bound to it

scenarios.title: Fetching an id nobody allocated raises
given: a Handle table
scenarios.when: an id it never allocated is fetched
scenarios.then: it raises

scenarios.title: The table has a ceiling and stops there
given: a Handle table filled to its highest id
scenarios.when: one more allocation is attempted
scenarios.then: it raises

scenarios.title: The ceiling is a property of the wire, not of the table
given: the Handle table's ceiling constant
scenarios.when: it is read
scenarios.then: it is the value the wire format fixes

scenarios.title: A reflective object is never given a reference
given: a Handle table
scenarios.when: a reflective gadget is offered for allocation
scenarios.then: it is refused

scenarios.title: A callable still gets one
given: a Handle table
scenarios.when: a callable is offered for allocation
scenarios.then: it is allocated

scenarios.title: A reference from an earlier invocation resolves to nothing
given: a reference issued by an earlier invocation's table
scenarios.when: the next invocation's table is asked for it
scenarios.then: it resolves to no object

scenarios.title: An id nobody was given resolves to nothing
given: an invocation's Handle table
scenarios.when: an arbitrary integer is presented as a reference
scenarios.then: it resolves to no object

scenarios.title: References minted during a failed wrap leave with their table
given: an invocation whose wrap failed partway
scenarios.when: the ids it had minted are presented afterward
scenarios.then: they resolve to no object

scenarios.title: The wire's own scalars are recognised as themselves
given: a value of each scalar kind the wire carries
scenarios.when: the walk classifies it
scenarios.then: it is recognised as wire-representable

scenarios.title: A reference is wire-representable
given: an existing capability reference
scenarios.when: the walk classifies it
scenarios.then: it is recognised as wire-representable

scenarios.title: An integer past the wire's width is not
given: an Integer outside the range the wire carries
scenarios.when: the walk classifies it
scenarios.then: it is refused

scenarios.title: Nor is a scalar the wire has no shape for
given: a scalar of a kind the wire does not carry
scenarios.when: the walk classifies it
scenarios.then: it is refused

scenarios.title: An Array is representable exactly when its elements are
given: an Array whose elements are all representable, and one where they are not
scenarios.when: the walk classifies each
scenarios.then: only the first is representable

scenarios.title: A Hash is representable exactly when its keys and values are
given: a Hash whose keys and values are all representable, and one where they are not
scenarios.when: the walk classifies each
scenarios.then: only the first is representable

scenarios.title: A representable value is left alone
given: a wire-representable value
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: it passes through unchanged

scenarios.title: A leaf the wire cannot carry is handed to the wrapper
given: a value the wire cannot carry
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: the wrapper is asked to reference it

scenarios.title: A mixed Array only wraps what needs wrapping
given: an Array holding both representable and non-representable elements
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: only the non-representable elements are referenced

scenarios.title: A Hash's values are walked and its keys are not
given: a Hash whose values need wrapping
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: the values are referenced and the keys pass through

scenarios.title: A key the wire cannot carry fails the invocation
given: a Hash keyed by a value the wire cannot carry
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: `Kobako::SandboxError` is raised

scenarios.title: A reference is not referenced again
given: a value already carrying a capability reference
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: the reference passes through unchanged

scenarios.title: Nesting is walked a level at a time
given: a container nested several levels deep
scenarios.when: the walk runs over it
scenarios.then: each level is walked in turn

scenarios.title: A value carrying no reference is restored as itself
given: a value holding no capability reference
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: it passes through unchanged

scenarios.title: A bare reference restores to its object
given: a capability reference with a live binding
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: it answers the bound object

scenarios.title: An Array restores only its references
given: an Array holding both references and ordinary values
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: only the references become objects

scenarios.title: A Hash restores on both sides
given: a Hash holding references as keys and as values
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: both sides become objects

scenarios.title: Nesting is restored a level at a time
given: a container nested several levels deep holding references
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: each level is restored in turn

scenarios.title: A reference with no live binding fails the invocation
given: a capability reference whose binding is gone
scenarios.when: the restore runs over it
scenarios.then: `Kobako::SandboxError` is raised

scenarios.title: A reference does not survive its invocation
given: a reference issued during an earlier invocation
scenarios.when: the next invocation presents it as a receiver
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: A reference does not travel between Sandboxes as a receiver
given: a reference issued by one Sandbox
scenarios.when: another Sandbox presents it as a receiver
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: Nor as an argument
given: a reference issued by one Sandbox
scenarios.when: another Sandbox passes it as an argument
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: A keyword name that is not a name is a wire violation
given: a dispatch whose keyword map is keyed by something other than a name
scenarios.when: the host reads it
scenarios.then: it answers as a wire violation

scenarios.title: An id the table never issued is refused at the dispatch
given: a dispatch naming a reference id the table never issued
scenarios.when: the host reads it
scenarios.then: it answers as an undefined target

scenarios.title: A call nested past the depth bound is contained
given: a dispatch nested past the depth the host accepts
scenarios.when: the host reads it
scenarios.then: it answers on the fault arm as an internal failure

scenarios.title: An answer the host cannot write is the Service's failure, not the wire's
given: a bound Service answering a value the host cannot encode
scenarios.when: the guest calls it
scenarios.then: the failure is attributed to the Service

scenarios.title: That failure is described in the host's own words
given: a bound Service answering a value the host cannot encode
scenarios.when: the guest reads the failure's message
scenarios.then: it is worded by the Host Gem rather than by the codec

scenarios.title: Running out of references while wrapping takes the fault arm
given: an invocation whose Handle table is exhausted
scenarios.when: a Service answers a value needing a new reference
scenarios.then: the dispatch answers on the fault arm

scenarios.title: That exhaustion surfaces as a Sandbox failure
given: an invocation whose Handle table is exhausted
scenarios.when: the guest leaves the failure unrescued
scenarios.then: `Kobako::SandboxError` is raised

scenarios.title: A failure the host was not meant to catch is not caught
given: a bound Service raising outside the ordinary error hierarchy
scenarios.when: the guest calls it
scenarios.then: that failure escapes the dispatcher's rescue

scenarios.title: A reference reaches the host as its object through a real invocation
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code passes the reference back as a positional argument
scenarios.then: the Service acts on the original host object

scenarios.title: And as a keyword argument
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code passes the reference back as a keyword argument
scenarios.then: the Service acts on the original host object

scenarios.title: And in both positions at once
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered stateful objects
scenarios.when: guest code passes references back positionally and by keyword together
scenarios.then: the Service acts on the original host objects

scenarios.title: And nested inside an Array argument
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code passes the reference back inside an Array
scenarios.then: the Service acts on the original host object

scenarios.title: And nested inside a keyword's Hash value
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code passes the reference back inside a keyword's Hash value
scenarios.then: the Service acts on the original host object

scenarios.title: A reference returned from the invocation becomes its object again
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code returns the reference as the invocation's value
scenarios.then: the host receives the original object

scenarios.title: Even nested in a container
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code returns the reference inside nested containers
scenarios.then: the host receives the original object in place

scenarios.title: Even standing as a Hash key
given: a Sandbox whose Service answered a stateful object
scenarios.when: guest code returns the reference as a Hash key
scenarios.then: the host receives the original object in that position

scenarios.title: And when it comes back through a yield block
given: a Sandbox whose Service yields to a guest block
scenarios.when: the block answers with a reference
scenarios.then: the Service receives the original object

scenarios.title: A reference the guest damaged still routes to its object
given: a Sandbox whose guest code altered what it holds around a reference
scenarios.when: it calls a method through that reference
scenarios.then: the original host object answers

scenarios.title: A brace-less keyword arrives as a keyword
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its keyword arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a brace-less keyword
scenarios.then: the Service receives it among its keywords

scenarios.title: An explicit Hash stays positional
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its positional arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with an explicit Hash literal
scenarios.then: the Service receives it among its positional arguments

scenarios.title: The two never mix
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading both argument kinds
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with an explicit Hash and a brace-less keyword together
scenarios.then: each arrives in its own bucket

scenarios.title: A splatted Hash arrives as keywords
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its keyword arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it splatting a Hash as keywords
scenarios.then: the Service receives them among its keywords

scenarios.title: Splatting nothing produces no keywords
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its keyword arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it splatting an empty Hash
scenarios.then: the Service receives no keywords

scenarios.title: A keyword whose value is a Hash is still a keyword
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its keyword arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a keyword whose value is a Hash
scenarios.then: the Service receives the keyword carrying that Hash

scenarios.title: An empty explicit Hash is still positional
given: a Sandbox with a Service reading its positional arguments
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with an empty explicit Hash literal
scenarios.then: the Service receives it among its positional arguments

scenarios.title: An entrypoint argument the wire cannot carry becomes a reference
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint that calls a method on its argument
scenarios.when: it runs with a stateful host object as a positional argument
scenarios.then: the guest reaches that object and the call answers

scenarios.title: And so does one passed by keyword
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint that calls a method on a keyword's value
scenarios.when: it runs with a stateful host object as a keyword value
scenarios.then: the guest reaches that object and the call answers

scenarios.title: An entrypoint argument keyed by an unwrappable value is refused
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: it runs with a Hash argument keyed by a value that cannot be referenced
scenarios.then: `Kobako::SandboxError` is raised

scenarios.title: An argument that refers to itself is refused
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: it runs with an argument containing itself
scenarios.then: `Kobako::SandboxError` is raised

scenarios.title: Dispatching survives collection pressure
given: a Sandbox under garbage-collection stress
scenarios.when: guest code dispatches repeatedly through references
scenarios.then: every dispatch answers

scenarios.title: So does unwinding out of a block under compaction
given: a Sandbox under garbage-collection compaction
scenarios.when: guest code breaks out of a yielded block
scenarios.then: the invocation answers the break's value

scenarios.title: A receiver-less guest idiom composes over references
given: a Sandbox whose Service answers child objects
scenarios.when: guest code builds a nested structure through a receiver-less idiom
scenarios.then: the host receives the structure the idiom described

scenarios.title: So does the block-parameter form
given: a Sandbox whose Service answers child objects
scenarios.when: guest code builds the same structure through a block parameter
scenarios.then: the host receives the structure the idiom described

scenarios.title: An idiom's vocabulary is the host's method set and no wider
given: a Sandbox whose guest idiom forwards any name to the host
scenarios.when: guest code calls a name the host object does not define
scenarios.then: `Kobako::ServiceError` is raised

scenarios.title: Both frontends route a dispatch the same way
given: a scenario whose guest calls a bound Service
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same answer

scenarios.title: Both make a Service's own failure rescuable the same way
given: a scenario whose bound Service raises and whose guest rescues it
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same rescued value

scenarios.title: Both refuse an unknown method the same way
given: a scenario calling a method the bound object does not define
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they refuse it the same way

scenarios.title: Both attribute an argument fault the same way
given: a scenario calling a bound Service with arguments it cannot accept
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they attribute the failure the same way

scenarios.title: Both narrow a host object the same way
given: a scenario whose bound object narrows its guest-reachable surface
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same reachable surface

scenarios.title: Both carry a reference through its life the same way
given: a scenario minting a reference, using it, and returning it
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same values

scenarios.title: Both refuse a reference the guest tried to mint
given: a scenario whose guest tries to construct a reference from an integer
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they refuse it the same way

scenarios.title: Both wrap an entrypoint's unwrappable argument the same way
given: a scenario running an entrypoint with a stateful host argument
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same answer

text: A guest call reaching a host object is the only route outward, so what it
carries is witnessed in both directions and at three depths: the walk that
decides what the wire can hold, the table that hands out references for what
it cannot, and the dispatch that puts them back together.
A reference lasts one invocation and belongs to one Sandbox. Both bounds are
witnessed as a receiver and as an argument, because a table consulted on one
path and not the other would pass either witness alone.
The two argument kinds are separated by how the guest wrote the call and not
by what the value is, so a Hash appears on both sides of that line — as a
positional literal, as a splatted keyword map, and as a keyword's value — and
Everything that answers on the fault arm rather than raising is here, since
the dispatcher never raises; what a Host App finally rescues is the error
